questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss it, drive to the next exit instead.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if someone is passing you. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
Where there is a red light.
When a traffic officer orders you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: Before you start the car, what should you check?

options.text: Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, make sure you and all your passengers have buckled your seat belts.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.
Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing lights. Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left on green that they do not have the right-of-way. You must wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never try to go around the gate.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what other cars are doing instead of listening to the guard.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow the directions of crossing guards and traffic officers in school zones. Drive slowly and carefully in school areas.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to prevent death or serious injury in a crash.

questions.question: Is drinking alcohol and driving a traffic safety problem?

options.text: No, it is a minor problem.
Yes, it is a serious problem.
No, it is safe if you have only had a few drinks.
No, it is only dangerous to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a serious problem.
questions.explanation: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is a serious safety threat. Alcohol makes safe driving impossible and endangers everyone on the road.

questions.question: Littering:

options.text: Is against the law.
May cause a traffic accident.
Can lead to a $1,000 fine and up to one year in jail.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Littering is illegal and looks bad. It can cause traffic accidents. For example, a lit cigarette thrown from your car can blow into the vehicle behind you and cause damage or injury. If found guilty of littering, you may pay up to $1,000 and/or spend up to one year in jail.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are making a turn.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive on any road.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: Directed to do so by a flagger.
It is controlled by a stop sign.
Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the chance of death in a crash increases. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is almost impossible. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may try dangerous moves to pass you.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway:

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and other drugs together can increase how much they affect you. For example, one drink with a cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks would affect you by themselves.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the laws that would be in place if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from signs, flaggers, or police officers in construction zones. Failing to do so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be coming. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the light turns red.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what other drivers are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop your vehicle unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop for any trains or vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do before making a turn?

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Turn the steering wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always turn on your signal three to four seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Keep extra distance between your vehicle and theirs.
Understand that this driver is not paying full attention to driving.
Do not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not drive while distracted by passengers, searching for items, reading, or daydreaming. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because accidents are more likely when drivers are not focused on the road.

questions.question: Which of these is a common cause of traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention to the road can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.
